scope: Roadman Cycling release covering the predict/[slug] fixture fallback, the /good-legs permanent redirect to /app, and the static TikTok domain verification file. The QA pass also repairs release-gate blockers in blog search retry state, event countdown animation state, and the Dragon Ride predictor mapping so the published build remains reviewable. The resulting reviewed fingerprint is the post-repair content digest; the originally requested fingerprint changed only because the release-blocking source repairs are included in this publish candidate.

sections.readerQuestion: Can a reader open a race predictor page when the dynamic predictor data store is unavailable or empty?
sections.usefulAnswer: Yes. The page now has a read-only fixture fallback for predictor course and report reads, while write paths stay unavailable outside the real backing store. The Dragon Ride route now maps to its predictor fixture so every listed predictor race is resolvable.
sections.evidence: Codex rendered /predict/ring-of-beara on desktop and mobile with HTTP 200, the expected race heading and no error overlay. Focused predictor fixture and report tests passed after adding the Dragon Ride predictor slug.
sections.editorialDecision: Publish the fallback because it preserves the existing reader-facing predictor experience during backend gaps without inventing results, accepting submissions, or changing race copy.

sections.readerQuestion: What happens when a visitor follows the old Good Legs URL?
sections.usefulAnswer: The legacy /good-legs path resolves to /app, keeping old links useful while the current Good Legs product page remains the canonical destination.
sections.evidence: Codex rendered /good-legs on desktop and mobile and observed the final URL as http://localhost:3000/app with HTTP 200, the Good Legs hero headline and no horizontal overflow.
sections.editorialDecision: Keep the redirect because it is navigational only and does not alter product promises, pricing or onboarding behaviour.

sections.readerQuestion: Does the TikTok verification artefact add public editorial or marketing content?
sections.usefulAnswer: No. The file is a single static verification token served from public assets, with no Roadman editorial wording, product claim or tracking flow.
sections.evidence: Codex requested the text file locally and verified HTTP 200 with the exact one-line token body and no additional markup or editorial content.
sections.editorialDecision: Publish the verification file as a technical ownership artefact only, separate from any editorial or product narrative.

claimsAndSources: The changed public claims are limited to route availability: predictor pages can render from existing fixture data, /good-legs redirects to the current app page, and TikTok can verify a static token. No performance, coaching, pricing, membership, medical, legal or availability claim was added.
examplesAndReasoning: The rendered examples cover the changed predictor surface, the legacy redirect and the token file. Focused tests cover predictor fixture completeness and report fallback behaviour, including the Dragon Ride mapping that previously broke the fixture completeness check.
voiceAndCuts: No article, podcast, sales or coaching copy was added. The only visible navigation change is the legacy redirect, and the verification file contains no brand voice beyond the external service token.
desktopReview: Codex rendered http://localhost:3000/predict/ring-of-beara and http://localhost:3000/good-legs at 1365 × 900. Both pages completed without a Next.js overlay or horizontal overflow; the predictor page showed the Ring of Beara heading and the Good Legs legacy path resolved to /app.
mobileReview: Codex rendered http://localhost:3000/predict/ring-of-beara and http://localhost:3000/good-legs at 390 × 844. Both pages completed without a Next.js overlay or horizontal overflow; the predictor heading and the Good Legs /app destination remained readable in the mobile viewport.
productAndOfferAccuracy: No product offer changed. The /app page content, predictor copy, purchase paths, forms and sign-up promises remain as already published; the TikTok file is ownership verification only.
